q: Which of the following is NOT considered normal in a newborn?
e: Central cyanosis (a blue tongue and lips) is always abnormal; the other options are normal findings in a newborn.

q: Which newborn finding is abnormal and needs investigation?
o: Skin dimple over the lower sacrum
e: A midline sacral dimple or tuft of hair may mark spina bifida occulta, so a spinal ultrasound is done.

q: A newborn girl has bilateral breast enlargement with a little milk. The next step is:
e: The swelling is caused by withdrawal of maternal hormones and settles in weeks. Squeezing the breasts causes mastitis.

q: All of the following reflexes are present at birth EXCEPT:
e: The parachute reaction appears at 8–9 months and persists for life.

q: At 36 hours a term baby has not passed meconium and has abdominal distension. The X-ray shows dilated loops of bowel and calcification in the scrotum. What is the most useful test?
e: Meconium ileus, with calcification from meconium peritonitis, suggests cystic fibrosis, so a sweat chloride test is done.

q: A term baby weighed 3.4 kg at birth and 3.15 kg on day 3, and is feeding well. What is the best action?
o: Reassure: the weight loss is within normal limits
e: A loss of 7% is normal (up to 10% is normal); the birth weight is regained by 10–14 days.

q: Which is given routinely to every newborn at birth to prevent bleeding?
e: Vitamin K 1 mg intramuscularly prevents vitamin K deficiency bleeding.

q: A newborn becomes cyanosed at rest and while feeding but turns pink when crying. A nasogastric tube cannot be passed. What is the diagnosis?
e: Newborns breathe through the nose; crying opens the mouth as an airway.

q: Which IMCI sign in a young infant needs urgent referral?
o: A weight loss of 5% on day 3
e: Movement only when stimulated is a danger sign of serious illness.

q: Bilateral absence of the Moro reflex in a newborn suggests:
o: Depression of the central nervous system
e: Absence on both sides indicates hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy, sepsis, kernicterus or drugs. Absence on one side indicates a fractured clavicle or Erb's palsy.
